#3172. Could SpaceX Be the Ultimate Winner of the Nvidia-Jensen Huang Split?

Terafab could be Jensen Huang's new home.

By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:00AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›

Few companies that have undergone more radical changes recently than Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), whose co-founder and chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, abruptly resigned earlier this month. Although there are calls from investors and employees to bring him back, the board of directors has stated that it has no interest in doing that.

Nobody knows for certain what Nvidia's future holds, and it may hinge on who fills the CEO role. However, there is another company that could benefit from this: Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%). SpaceX is a client of Nvidia's, so how can it benefit?

Well, SpaceX's CEO, Elon Musk, has already made it publicly known that he would love to have Huang run his Terafab division, the company’s huge factory designed to build compute hardware. That would certainly bring on an excellent technology leader who knows the industry inside and out, but there are no official reports that this is being considered at this time.

So, can SpaceX still benefit from all of this? Let's take a look.

Terafab is SpaceX's semiconductor manufacturing project in Texas. Both SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA -7.64%) are involved in it, along with Intel (INTC -7.97%). Should Terafab come into existence, its primary competitor would be Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM -9.48%).

Taiwan Semiconductor is a semiconductor manufacturer that supplies the world with the vast majority of advanced chips. Companies like SpaceX and Tesla cannot get enough chips fast enough, so they are looking to build their own fabrication facilities to replace them. Terafab also integrates memory chip production, so companies like Micron (MU -13.89%) are also in competition with Terafab. Terafab would only supply chips to SpaceX and Tesla, so it wouldn’t challenge Taiwan Semiconductor or Micron for sales to their other customers.

Chip production is no easy business, and countless advanced technologies are difficult to replicate and take years of knowledge. But if a large amount of knowledge could be imported via Jensen Huang, then Terafab could have a shot at success.

Still, it's important to remember that while Huang ran a chip company, the company was mostly centered on design. Nvidia only designs graphics processing units (GPUs), the computing engines inside data centers; it doesn’t manufacture them. Although designing high-tech products requires knowing how they are made, there is a difference between knowing a process and having hands-on experience doing it and troubleshooting it when things go wrong. Huang's knowledge would be a game changer for SpaceX and Tesla, but it may not be enough to crack into this industry.

Although Huang may be a top option for the job, this is still another bold business launch by Musk, and it will be years before this facility is operational.

So, can SpaceX really benefit from Huang’s absence at Nvidia?

There's no doubt that Jensen Huang shaped the design path of Nvidia. The whole world benefited from his prescience and leadership, whether they know it or not, and his shoes will be hard, if not impossible, to fill.

Depending on who is selected as the next CEO of Nvidia, the technical visionary mindset needs to be replicated; otherwise, Nvidia won't be the same company. This is a huge risk for any company that is currently deploying Nvidia products, such as SpaceX.

SpaceX informed investors during its Q2 conference call that it is exclusively using Nvidia products for the foreseeable future. Musk made that decision because Nvidia's new Rubin architecture is best in class. That technology won't change with Huang not in the CEO role, so SpaceX will likely continue to deploy Nvidia hardware.

So, at the end of the day, unless Huang chooses to lead Terafab for Musk, SpaceX is likely better off with Huang in the CEO role at Nvidia. The same could be said of a whole host of other AI companies that use Nvidia products. But with Nvidia’s board declaring that there is no path for return, it seems likely that Huang’s future lies elsewhere.

#3171. I’ve tested Ubuntu 27.04 ahead of its April release – and it will wow you

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

I've been using Ubuntu 27.04, and the speed boost is noticeable. Here's what else is coming.

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful

With the repository added, you can install it with:

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

#3170. Google Gemini Partners With Watch Duty to Clear Static From Firefighter Radio

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

After spending months training with firefighters in the field, the app uses Google Gemini to decode distorted radio signals in real time.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

On Friday, Google’s Gemini team announced the results of a new partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

The Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to update maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

“This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” said Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google says the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

One metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

The Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

The integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

#3167. Don’t Miss Out on GTA 6 Launch Week: Here’s How to Take Rockstar’s New Game Anywhere

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Whether you’re on a work trip, vacationing or otherwise indisposed, there are a few good options to scratch your Grand Theft Auto itch on the go.

Look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may currently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

If you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

If you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

The PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

Microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing new game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

#3166. What Will Anthropic’s Price Be in 3 Months? History Offers an Answer That’s Strikingly Clear.

The stock climbed 17% on its first day of trading.

By Adria Cimino – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:02AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) soared onto the scene this week with the biggest initial public offering on record, raising more than $81 billion. This figure climbed to $93.5 billion as underwriters exercised an overallotment option. Anthropic opened at $111 on its first day of trading, representing a 33% gain from its IPO price of $83. The stock finished the day off its peak, however, with a 17% increase.

Investors kept a close eye on the Anthropic IPO as it represented the first pure-play artificial intelligence (AI) company to debut on the market -- and could offer insight into general sentiment regarding the AI space. AI stocks led major indexes higher in recent years as investors cheered the technology's game-changing potential. This year, however, concern has grown about the depth of tech companies' spending on the AI build-out. Investors have questioned whether the revenue opportunity will support the hundreds of billions of dollars invested and whether this pace of investment is sustainable.

After Anthropic's explosive debut, you may be wondering what the stock price will be in three months. History offers an answer that's strikingly clear.

First, though, let's take a quick look at the Anthropic story so far. Anthropic, founded by Dario Amodei and a team of former OpenAI researchers in 2021, is the maker of popular AI model Claude. The company has seen revenue roar higher ever since Claude's initial launch just three years ago. Over that time period, it's gone from about zero to more than $17 billion in the latest quarter.

Anthropic fits into the AI ecosystem in the following way: It partners with major cloud providers for the enormous compute it needs to train its Claude models, then monetizes Claude through serving companies and consumers. Enterprise, however, is a key focus for Anthropic, and more than 50% of the Fortune 500 brought in at least $100,000 in revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of the end of September.

Now, let's consider our question: What will the Anthropic stock price be three months after this historic IPO? For an idea, I looked at 10 of the biggest IPOs from 1999 through 2023, including names such as Meta Platforms and Uber Technologies. In their first three months of trading, eight delivered a negative performance. And five of those declines were in the double digits. In fact, the average three-month return was a 13% decline.

Two recent IPO stocks, Space Exploration Technologies and Cerebras Systems, confirm that trend. They fell 6% and 29%, respectively, in their first three months of trading.

So, history offers us a strikingly clear answer: If Anthropic follows the trend, the stock may drop over the coming three months, potentially even in the double digits.

What does this mean for you as an investor? If you're already an Anthropic shareholder, this isn't a reason to sell. Short-term performance isn't important; what's more important is a company's earnings and stock performance over a number of years.

As for whether you should buy Anthropic, my answer is the following: I wouldn't rush to get in on the stock. The AI lab offers an impressive growth story, but it still comes with a hefty amount of risk. This includes the investment required to continue building and training models and other potential problems such as any slowdown in demand or competition from rivals like OpenAI. Questions about possible regulation of the industry could also weigh on stock performance.

All of this means you should take your time evaluating Anthropic, and if you feel the stock suits your investment style, consider buying on an eventual dip.

#3163. iOS 27.3 Could Bring the Redesigned Health App and a More Capable Siri AI to Your Device Soon

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems

The Health app overhaul and new Apple Intelligence features lead the latest public beta.

Apple launched the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the new Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS update in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a new Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by new audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

While both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I said, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just said.

Siri AI gets a huge update in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

You can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

StandBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

Apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

If you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a new setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

If you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have new options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

Next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

Those are a few of the new features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

#3162. President Donald Trump's Economy and the AI-Driven Stock Market Are in Trouble, Thanks to a Newly Identified Source of Inflation

Elevated inflation is no longer just a Trumpflation story.

By Sean Williams – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:06AM EST

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›

The stock market has endured some of its most volatile days in history under President Donald Trump. Nevertheless, the iconic Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.93%), benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%), and tech-fueled Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) have averaged higher returns under Trump than under most other presidents since the late 1890s.

Some of this outperformance can be traced directly to Trump's policies. The signing of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act into law in December 2017 slashed the peak marginal corporate income tax rate from 35% to 21%, leading to record share buybacks by S&P 500 companies.

But the bulk of Wall Street's gains comes courtesy of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution and the ongoing AI data center build-out. AI is the largest addressable opportunity investors have ever seen, which explains why the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite have blasted to several record highs.

Persistently elevated inflation is a serious problem for President Trump's economy and Wall Street. Image source: Official White House Photo by Andrea Hanks, courtesy of the National Archives.

But if things ever seem too good to be true on Wall Street, caveat emptor!

Both President Trump's economy and the AI-driven stock market are in trouble, with persistently elevated inflation to blame. If Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) get aggressive with interest rate hikes, it would likely spell the end of a four-year (and counting) bull market.

The issue is that elevated inflation is no longer just a Trumpflation story. The central bank has identified a new source of inflation that's put FOMC policymakers in quite the pickle.

Keep in mind that when the U.S. economy is growing, a modest level of inflation is expected. It's a positive thing when strong demand for goods and services gives businesses some degree of pricing power.

But the theme of 2026 has been one of persistently elevated inflation. Whereas the FOMC aims for a "timely return" to the 2% long-term inflation target, Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, reached a three-year high of 4.1% in May and has been moving in the wrong direction, yet again, in recent months.

Trumpflation (i.e., inflation driven by the president's policies) is certainly to blame for some of this pricing pressure.

New from the New York Fed: "By February 2026, tariffs had contributed 2.9 pp to goods price inflation, and without them goods prices would have fallen slightly." About one quarter of every point in higher tariff rates shows up in consumer prices within one year. • A 10% across-the-board tariff yields a 2.6% rise in consumer goods prices after one year. • About two thirds of the increase comes from pricier imports, which get passed through quickly. • Another third comes from U.S. made goods, as producers face higher input costs and less import competition. This takes longer, about 6-12 months, to filter through.

Donald Trump's tariff and trade policy has been one clearly defined source of elevated inflation since the start of his second nonconsecutive term. Following the April 2025 "Liberation Day" tariffs, which the U.S. Supreme Court struck down in February 2026, the Trump administration has imposed sweeping global duties of 10% to 12.5% on more than 80 countries.

According to a recent report from three New York Federal Reserve economists writing for Liberty Street Economics ("How Fast Do Tariffs Pass Through into Consumer Prices?"), Trump's 2025 tariffs added an estimated 2.9 percentage points to goods price inflation by February 2026. Goods prices would have fallen if not for the president's tariffs.

The Trump-led Iran war is also pushing up prices. The Strait of Hormuz is a global crude oil choke point, and its closure has resulted in the largest energy supply disruption in modern history. Diesel prices climbed to an all-time high in September.

A slow but steady rise in Core PCE, which removes volatile food and energy costs, also suggests that Iran-war-driven inflation has reached the broader economy. The added transportation and supply chain expenses associated with the Iran war are translating into higher costs for consumers.

The newest source of inflation has put Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the FOMC in a pickle. Image source: Official Federal Reserve Photo.

But Trumpflation is no longer the only driver of elevated inflation. Beginning in June and in each subsequent FOMC meeting, Fed Chair Warsh and his colleagues have homed in on a new source of inflation -- one that may prove incredibly challenging to combat.

The FOMC's minutes for the June meeting contained the following statement:

That's right, folks... the AI infrastructure build-out, Wall Street's and the U.S. economy's No. 1 catalyst, is now officially a culprit for elevated inflation.

*KASHKARI: INFLATION DRIVEN BY SUPPLY ISSUES, INCLUDING AI-BUILD Here we go: AI as source of inflation

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite wouldn't be where they are today without businesses spending a jaw-dropping amount of capital on AI hardware. A combination of otherworldly demand for data center infrastructure and ongoing supply shortages for graphics processing units and memory is affording AI hardware companies never-before-seen pricing power and record-high margins.

Likewise, the AI revolution is a key economic growth driver. President Trump favors as little regulation as possible to enable this infrastructure build-out.

However, rapidly rising prices for electronic components are adversely affecting consumers and businesses. Any device with a central processing unit, memory, or storage has likely endured a price hike. This means higher costs for smartphones, laptops, and other devices.

The AI boom is transforming one of the biggest deflationary forces into a key source of US inflation: Import prices for computer and electronic products surged +7.4% in the first 6 months of 2026, to 77.1 points, the highest since January 2016. This also marks a +8.0% YoY jump, the largest annual increase on record. This represents a historic reversal from a downtrend which persisted for over two decades. Between 2006 and 2019, computer and electronic product import prices fell -30%, as improving technology and manufacturing efficiency consistently pushed costs lower. Now, the AI investment boom is straining manufacturing capacity for semiconductors, servers, and electronic components, as companies race to build out AI infrastructure regardless of cost. The AI revolution has flipped technology from a long-term source of deflation into a major driver of inflation.

If Fed Chair Warsh and his colleagues maintain their focus on price stability and aggressively raise interest rates to do so, they could effectively cut off the stock market's and economy's No. 1 catalyst at the knees. Increasing borrowing costs for a partially debt-financed AI build-out would almost certainly slow this expansion, hurting growth projections and calling into question valuations amid the second-priciest stock market in history.

If the Fed does nothing, it could eventually prove just as damaging for Trump's economy and the AI-driven bull market, with inflation continuing to march higher.

Regardless of the solution, the economy and Wall Street appear likely to pay the price.

If Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The company already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer

“You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets users view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. #3157. Should You Really Buy Anthropic Stock After Its Historic IPO? History Offers a Clear Answer.

Anthropic just completed the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history in terms of capital raised.

By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:24AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Anthropic (ANT -8.50%), the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, made history when it went public on Nov. 19. Its initial public offering (IPO) raised a record $81.3 billion, topping the $75 billion raised by Space Exploration Technologies in June.Anthropic priced its stock at $83, implying a valuation of about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis (which includes items such as stock options), according to The Wall Street Journal. Shares opened around $111.50 and briefly moved higher before closing around $97. But the stock plummeted 9% on Nov. 20, bringing the price back to $89.

Is Anthropic a smart investment right now?

Image source: OpenAI (AI-generated illustration).

Companies often go public when enthusiasm is high, allowing them to command rich valuations. But the initial excitement generally fades as investors shift their focus to financial fundamentals. That can lead to sharp declines, especially among companies that go public with particularly large market values.

The table below lists the 10 largest U.S. IPOs since 2016, ranked by market value at the IPO price. For each stock, it shows the first-year return and the largest decline from the IPO price during that period.

Data source: BlackRock, YCharts. SpaceX is marked with an asterisk because one year has not elapsed since the IPO, so the figures are subject to change.

As shown above, among the 10 largest U.S. IPOs in the last decade, the median stock fell 46% from its IPO price at some point during the first year, and it finished the first year 16% below its IPO price.

What does that mean? Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share. If the stock's performance matches the historical median, it will decline to $45 per share (46% below the IPO price) at some point during the first year, and it will finish the first year around $70 per share (16% below the IPO price).

Readers may think a buy-and-hold strategy will compensate for initial losses, but history suggests otherwise. Since their respective IPOs, the 10 stocks listed in the table have underperformed the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) by an average of 48 percentage points. In other words, investors who bought an S&P 500 index fund rather than those stocks at their IPO prices would have earned much better returns on average.

Here's the big picture: History says Anthropic stock could fall sharply during the first year, and investors that purchase shares around the IPO price may underperform the S&P 500 over the long term. Of course, how shares actually perform depends on investor sentiment and the company's financial fundamentals.

Anthropic is a formidable player in artificial intelligence. Its Claude models compete with products from OpenAI and Alphabet, while its growing enterprise business positions the company to benefit as organization integrate AI into everyday workflows. The company also has relationships with major technology companies, such as Amazon and Google, that provide access to computing infrastructure and distribution opportunities.

However, Anthropic operates in a very competitive industry where technological leadership can change quickly. The company must continually invest in increasingly sophisticated AI models and expensive computing infrastructure to keep pace with competitors that have tremendous financial resources. Those pressures could make it difficult to translate rapid revenue growth into sustainable profits.

Valuation adds another layer of risk. Anthropic currently has a market value of roughly $1.6 trillion. If we divide that figure by the trailing-12-month revenue of $35.3 billion, the stock has a price-to-sales ratio of 45. For context, only one stock in the S&P 500 currently has a more expensive valuation: Palantir Technologies currently trades at 47 times sales.

Here's the big picture: Anthropic has established a strong position in an industry with tremendous growth potential, but maintaining that position will require substantial investment, raising questions about its long-term profitability. Those concerns, coupled with a lofty valuation, could push the stock below its IPO price during the first year of trading. For now, I think investors would be wise to wait for a more attractive buying opportunity.

Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.

By default, most AI chatbots have a setting on by default that allows them to be trained on the conversations you have. This is the first and likely the most important setting you need to disable. Here’s how to turn it off.

The settings essentially remain the same across web, iOS and Android:

You may not see this option because with some accounts, like Enterprise plans, Claude doesn’t automatically collect this data. So if you have a Claude account through work, you might not have to worry about this.

While you’re at it, if you’re a Claude Code user, these settings will let you delete Code sessions stored on Anthropic’s server without deleting local sessions on your computer.

If you’ve ever shared a chat with anyone, you can also delete those chats in this menu as well.

Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training

Anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

According to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.)

The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

Like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

If you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:

This will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

To prevent Claude from creating new memories from your conversations:

If you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

However, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > iOS

The new Google Wallet app brings Gemini agentic shopping to US-based iOS users - sorry, no tap-to-pay.

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits

The new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Meta's 2026 sustainability report isn't a glowing review, thanks to AI.

Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Big Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the company is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”

It’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, said in 2023 that the company’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”

Meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the company says. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

Take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its new data center designs compared to its original ones.

But, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The company also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

#3152. NuScale Stock Has Lost 93% of Its Value. I'm Still Not Buying It.

The reactor developer now sells for less than its cash. Why isn't this a bargain?

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:29AM EST

10 stocks we like better than NuScale Power ›

A share of NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) cost $53.43 at the close on Oct. 15, 2025, the stock's highest finish ever. On Thursday, Nov. 19, the shares ended the day at $3.81 -- a fall of about 93% for the small modular reactor developer, and the stock's lowest close since early March 2024.

NuScale ended September sitting on about $1.86 billion in cash and investments, with no debt. At Thursday's close, the market priced the whole company at around $1.6 billion (including both its share classes), or over $200 million less than that cash. And because NuScale loses money every quarter, there's no price-to-earnings ratio to weigh against it.

For a stock that's lost almost all its value, that might look like a floor. Unfortunately, I don't think it's one.

The fact that would make NuScale worth owning hasn't changed throughout the slide: the company still doesn't have a firm order for its power modules.

NuScale has stayed busy. In October, it signed a contract with a manufacturer in South Korea to make a key piece of its first power module, the upper reactor coolant system.

But it's building that module without a customer.

Over 14 months ago, the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) and ENTRA1 Energy, NuScale's commercialization partner, signed a non-binding agreement for up to 6 gigawatts of new nuclear power. There's still no binding deal. NuScale's third-quarter earnings presentation says ENTRA1 is still in talks with TVA toward a definitive power purchase agreement.

Even a signed TVA deal wouldn't require anybody to buy NuScale's modules. NuScale's 2025 agreement with ENTRA1 names it a key supplier for ENTRA1's projects, but ENTRA1 has full discretion over whether to buy from NuScale at all.

"Once we have an order, we work on an OEM agreement, we'll have further clarity on margins," CFO Ramsey Hamady said on NuScale's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 5.

Showing how little NuScale is selling in the meantime, its third-quarter revenue was $281,000, down from $8.2 million a year ago. The first two quarters of 2026 brought in just around $640,000 in total.

Revenue has sat near zero all year, after the company's engineering work for a planned plant in Romania finished in late 2025. And NuScale doesn't expect the Romanian project's owner to sign its next contract before it lines up financing.

Not for me. A stock selling under its cash can look like a textbook value stock. But NuScale's cash might shrink a lot before an order ever comes along.

Setting aside a one-time payment of around $260 million to ENTRA1, NuScale's operations have burned about $47 million of cash a quarter so far this year. And spending is climbing. Third-quarter research and development expenses grew 63% year over year to $18.0 million as NuScale worked on its module components, and its operating loss of $64.8 million was up from $57.5 million in the first quarter. Granted, management expects to recover those component costs through payments under a future equipment agreement. That agreement doesn't exist yet, either.

Even more cash is set to leave under the ENTRA1 agreement. A binding power deal for ENTRA1 triggers a second payment from NuScale to ENTRA1, equal to 35% of the total. The first payment, which came due when ENTRA1 signed the non-binding TVA deal, was 15%.

Put simply, the next step forward would cost NuScale cash before it takes any in.

New share sales are the other way cash per share can shrink. NuScale raised around $1 billion from selling new stock earlier this year, boosting its Class A share count 29% from the end of 2025. And with a $750 million stock-sale program in place since August, it can keep adding shares over time.

Current cash per share, in short, likely isn't the cash per share shareholders wind up with.

Is NuScale stock a buy after losing 93% of its value? I don't think so.

Yes, a binding TVA deal could push the growth stock sharply higher for a while. But it would also trigger that second payment to ENTRA1. And until NuScale signs an equipment contract, investors can't gauge what it might make per module.

What would change my mind is a signed order for NuScale's modules, with enough disclosure of pricing and costs to demonstrate the margins Hamady described. I'd be willing to pay a higher valuation for the stock when that contract exists. Until then, I'm not buying shares, even at a price below NuScale's cash.

#3151. 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

In today's job market, do applicants really have a choice of whether to comply with AI hiring tools?

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report shows how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead

Samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”

#3150. Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Encryption can't protect your messages from an AI agent peeking over your shoulder.

Don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

Whittaker said that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the company is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

The problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal says that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

Whittaker said the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how big tech AI agents work.

“Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker said. “This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”

In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

“So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” said Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

Strand said the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand said.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

#3149. This Dividend ETF Could Supercharge Your Passive Income. Here's How.

Most income investors trade growth for yield. This ETF lets you have both.

By Keith Speights – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:44AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Goldman Sachs ETF Trust - Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Premium Income ETF ›

Many income investors view the trade-off between high yields and growth potential as a necessary evil. They think having both is virtually impossible.

However, that doesn't have to be the case. The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF (GPIX -3.38%) offers both high yields and growth. This dividend ETF could be the passive income and growth engine that many investors didn't know existed.

Like several top S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) index funds, the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF provides exposure to the S&P 500. Its top holdings include the largest components of the S&P 500 index itself: Apple (AAPL -1.90%), Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%), Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Amazon (AMZN -4.10%), and Alphabet (GOOG -2.59%) (GOOGL -2.70%).

But this isn't an ordinary S&P 500 ETF. Two words in the fund's name hint at what sets it apart: "Premium Income." The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF paid a distribution yield of 8.3% over the last 12 months. That's roughly eight times the yields offered by the State Street SPDR® S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY -3.64%) and the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%).

How does this ETF generate such juicy distributions? It uses a dynamic options "overwrite" strategy. What that means is that the Goldman Sachs fund sells call options on some, but not all, of its equity investments -- usually between 25% and 75%.

The fund's managers sell more call options to generate greater premium income when they view the market's upside as limited. And they dial back the option selling when they expect the stock market to rally.

This approach allows the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF to generate both growth and income. Since its inception in October 2023, the fund has delivered an average annual total return of 20.4%, not far below the S&P 500's 22.7%. But it has also given shareholders significantly higher income than the S&P 500 has.

The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF isn't the ideal choice for investors seeking only growth. Buying a traditional S&P 500 index fund would provide more growth than this ETF will.

However, this Goldman Sachs fund could be very attractive to income investors seeking some growth as icing on the cake. An initial investment of $100,000 would generate over $8,000 in annual income at the ETF's current distribution yield. And the initial $100,000 is likely to grow over the long term.

The cost of buying the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF is admittedly higher than the costs of investing in traditional S&P 500 index funds. But with a net annual expense ratio of 0.29%, the costs won't eat too much into your total returns. This annual expense ratio is also slightly lower than those of some covered call ETFs, such as the JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPQ -5.20%).

One key thing to note is that where investors hold this ETF could make a difference come tax time. The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF's distributions consist of ordinary income and return of capital (which isn't taxed when received, but lowers the cost basis, which can increase capital gains when you sell). In the fund's latest fiscal year, the return-of-capital component of the distributions was roughly 91%.

All investments come with risk. The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF is no exception. If the stock market tanks, so will this fund's share price.

That said, this dividend ETF is a genuine passive income supercharger. Investors should be able to count on high yields over time, along with long-term growth, thanks to its dynamic options overwrite strategy.

#3148. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Officially Heading to Mars

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

No space agency has ever staged spacecraft in orbit for a year before sending them on to Mars.

NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Typically, spacecraft use a planet or the sun’s natural gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the official debut of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the company was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

#3146. Social Security Retirees Get a Big COLA in 2027, but Benefits Will Increase Most in These 10 States

Social Security benefits and COLAs are indirectly influenced by the state of residence.

By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:48AM EST

Social Security is a critical source of income for millions of older Americans. Nearly 72 million people receive Social Security benefits, including more than 55 million retirees. And according to Gallup, nearly 9 in 10 of those retired workers depend on Social Security to some degree.

That makes annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) particularly important. These automatic pay increases are designed to protect the purchasing power of Social Security payments against inflation, helping retirees keep pace with rising prices.

Fortunately, Social Security recipients will get a relatively large raise in 2027. Benefits will increase 3.6%, up from the 2.8% COLA in 2026. The increase is also slightly larger than the 3.4% average COLA over the preceding decade.

Importantly, while all Social Security payments will increase by the same percentage next year, the extra income will vary widely when measured in dollars. Read on to see the 10 states in which retired workers will receive the largest COLAs in 2027.

Image source: OpenAI (AI-generated illustration).

Social Security's annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) are based on a subset of the Consumer Price Index known as the CPI-W. Specifically, the CPI-W from the third quarter (July to September) of the current year is compared with the average from the same period in the prior year, and the percentage increase becomes the COLA for the next year.

Social Security's COLA in 2027 will be 3.6%. The Social Security Administration estimates the average monthly retired-worker benefit will increase from $2,095 before the COLA to $2,170 after the COLA, meaning the average retired worker will receive an additional $75 per month or $900 for the full year.

To be clear, all retirees will receive the exact same 3.6% pay increase, but those with larger benefits will receive larger COLAs when measured in nominal dollars. To that end, retirees in the 10 states with the highest median Social Security benefits will receive some of the largest pay increases next year.

The table below shows the 10 states with the highest median Social Security benefits for retired workers as of December 2025, according to the Social Security Administration.

Data source: Social Security Administration, Annual Statistical Supplement, 2026, Table 5.J6.

Importantly, a retiree's state of residence has no direct impact on the amount of Social Security benefits they receive, but there is an indirect relationship. Benefits are primarily based on lifetime earnings and claiming age, so states with high median household incomes are likely to have high median Social Security benefits.

Indeed, six states listed in the table above -- New Jersey, New Hampshire, Maryland, Washington, Massachusetts, and Utah -- rank among the 10 states with the highest median income, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. And three others -- Connecticut, Delaware, and Minnesota -- have median incomes above the national median.

What about the other state? Michigan ranks among the 10 states with the highest median Social Security benefits despite having a median household income below the national median. That could mean more workers in Michigan claim Social Security at older ages, which results in larger benefits. Alternatively, workers with relatively high lifetime earnings may choose to retire in Michigan.

Here's the bottom line: Social Security benefits are not directly linked to where a retired worker lives, so moving to a different state will not automatically increase your monthly payments. Rather, workers in certain states tend to earn more money, often reflecting differences in local labor markets and living costs. And because Social Security benefits are based partly on lifetime earnings, those workers generally qualify for larger payments when they retire.
